# PR — 280_R6FIX.17 (BL-115): `provisionPersonalAccount` rides one tx with a per-user advisory lock

**Base:** `main` @ `3a840396` · **Branch:** `stevevitali/r6fix-17-provision-tx` · **mergePolicy:** OPERATOR

## Summary

BL-115 (277_R6LOW.1 sweep): `provisionPersonalAccount` was a check-then-write race — an
unguarded pre-read, then five independent pooled writes (`billing_accounts` → `provisionTrial`
→ `workspaces` → `workspace_members` → `is_test`). Two concurrent provisions of one user
(signup admission vs Better Auth `onUserCreate`, or a double-submit) both passed the pre-read
and double-inserted — two billing accounts, two `kind='personal'` workspaces, two memberships —
forking the session→principal `limit 1` join; a mid-provision failure also orphaned
billing/trial rows.

- The provision now rides ONE transaction through the existing `TxRunner` seam:
  `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(userId))` serializes concurrent provisions per user, the
  in-tx re-check returns the racing winner's rows, and all four writes commit-or-rollback
  together (`provisionTrial` included — trial rows are inside the atomic set).
- `txRunner` was already wired at both call sites — `createSignupRoutes` forwards it through
  `admitSignup`; `onUserCreate` passes the same variable `createShowcaseSeeder` already uses.
- `is_test` flag + Showcase seed stay post-commit (each carries its own tx; the seed must see
  committed rows). No schema change, no new client, no widened system seams.

## Test plan

- `apps/api/src/signup.test.ts` — three new PGlite pins: sequential double-provision idempotent
  (one workspace/billing row); the lock is the first in-tx statement keyed on the user id with
  the re-check ordered after it (mechanism pin — the session-scoped lock serializes across the
  pool's distinct connections in prod; it cannot block on PGlite's single wire, stated honestly);
  injected mid-provision failure rolls back all four row types.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/api/src/signup.test.ts` — 25/25 · `@rhema/api` typecheck + lint clean
  · append-only + build-memory checks run.
